title: An adjective before a plural noun

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: An adjective directly before a noun never changes, even when the noun is plural: *a nagy asztalok*. Only the noun carries the plural. After the noun the adjective takes the plural instead: *az asztalok nagyok*. Same words, two positions, two patterns.

items.spanish: A nagy asztalok és a kicsi székek.
items.english: The big tables and the small chairs.

items.spanish: A székek kicsik, az asztalok nagyok.
items.english: The chairs are small, the tables are big.

sections.content: Notice *nagy* and *kicsi* do not change in *a nagy asztalok és a kicsi székek*, even though both nouns are plural. That is very different from Spanish or French, where the adjective would take a plural ending too.
